title: CNN-measured tau tangle burden is linked to cognitive impairment in PART
summary: In 706 post-mortem brains from elderly people with mild or no amyloid plaques, a convolutional neural network trained to segment neurofibrillary tangles on p-tau-stained hippocampal sections gave tangle counts, positive pixel density and a graph-theory spatial metric. Several of these metrics predicted antemortem cognitive impairment in the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex (p < 0.0001); controlling for age, tangle counts remained significant (p = 0.04). Braak stage did not predict impairment. This is a retrospective association, and CNN validation details are not in the abstract.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network segmenting neurofibrillary tangles on p-tau stained hippocampus sections
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

evidence.tested: Retrospective autopsy cohort of 706 brains compared with antemortem cognitive status.
evidence.unknown: CNN accuracy against pathologists is not stated in the abstract; association only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN segmented tangles to give quantitative burden metrics beyond Braak staging.
